founderAuthorization.rule: Founder rule 2026-09-29: A blocked/review-pending package blocks ONLY its own dependency lane; implement the next independent eligible package in an isolated branch, validate, checkpoint, commit, prepare the frozen review bundle, mark it REVIEW_PENDING if Codex is unavailable, and continue; never modify a pending package's branch, bundle, clone, evidence or cycle state.
founderAuthorization.constraint: Tests and non-protected documentation only; no protected file, no pending package scope, no merge.

rationale: audit/KNOWN-TARGET-MACHINE-PENDING.md listed Windows process lock / kill / crash / restart / resume tests as pending; this package runs them on the target machine with real child processes for the process lock and the unattended orchestrator.
scenarios: a killed lock holder leaves a same-host dead-PID lock that is taken over; the live holder is detected first
five concurrent invocations produce exactly one winner
unreadable and foreign-host locks stay fail-closed and are not cleared

a real worker process running the production review executor (createExecutors, canonical command contracts, real git; only the Codex broker is replaced by an instrumented provider substitute that appends every call to a durable counter shared across workers) completes the provider call and governed evaluation and is killed before the outcome is persisted; after lease expiry a second worker process takes over, recovers the in-flight action, adopts the completed review and closes the package with exactly one measured invocation

the durable state of a crash after the provider call but before governed evaluation (evaluation artefacts removed) is resumed by evaluating the completed output in place without a new provider call; this scenario fails against the pre-hardening AUT1 code (PROVIDER_INVOKED_2_TIMES)
negative control: when the completion evidence is lost the restarted worker calls the provider again and the measurement reports PROVIDER_INVOKED_2_TIMES
a corrupted main state file falls back to the previous copy, the log stays verifiable and the chain continues

F-T1-001.observed: The crash/resume scenario initialised the provider-call count to the expected value after the kill and fabricated completion in parent memory; the injected executor guaranteed adoption, so production recovery was never exercised.
F-T1-001.fix: The scenario now runs the production review executor in real worker processes with an instrumented provider substitute and a durable invocation counter shared across workers; the first worker is killed after the provider call and before outcome persistence, the restarted worker adopts via the production path, and the test asserts exactly one measured invocation. A second scenario covers a crash before governed evaluation, and a negative control shows that a duplicate invocation fails the measurement. Checking the real path exposed a production gap (a completed but unevaluated run was not adopted); it is fixed in the rebased PKG-AUT1 commit b070dcb.
F-T1-001.retest: scripts/windows-crash-resume-selftest.mjs PASS 7/7; the before-evaluation scenario fails against the pre-hardening AUT1 code with PROVIDER_INVOKED_2_TIMES and passes with b070dcb; tests/pkg-t1-windows-crash-resume.test.ts asserts the three scenarios by name.
